design_rationale:
WHY THIS MAKES A GOOD TEST. The caller asks for one thing — close my stay off and take the balance — and the desk has to find, from the published terms and the folio alone, that three separate things are still owed or unspent before that balance can be struck: the supplement for the fifth adult sharing two rooms, the statutory tax nobody has posted on four nights of room money, and the property credit that will be forfeited at departure if it is not drawn down by the guest himself. None of the four figures can be looked up. Each is built from a different corner of the same folio, and the three writes that precede the settlement each change what the settlement reads. The tool layer refuses nothing, so an agent that closes the stay off first gets a cheerful receipt and a wrong terminal hash.

STEP 0 DRAW (scripts/draw_counts.py env/online_travel_agency/tasks/hotel_reservations_desk --task 1):
{"task": 1, "key": "online_travel_agency/hotel_reservations_desk/1", "prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [6, 4, 4, 4]}
The tree therefore has exactly three prerequisite problems besides the root, and the four computations take 6, 4, 4 and 4 factors. The root, stay_ext_departure_balance_settlement, takes 6; stay_ext_occupancy_supplement, stay_ext_statutory_tax_charge and stay_ext_resort_credit_application take 4 each. At least max(3-1, 1) = 2 edges must be value_input; all three are.

SCOPE. Occupied by task 0: stay_ext_late_cancellation_penalty and stay_ext_cancellation_refund_payout, with the tools confirm_reservation_cancellation_70c0f3f0 and raise_cancellation_refund_payout_a740a404, on the subjects stay_cancellation_charge and stay_refund_payout — the giving-up side of the product. Claimed here: stay_ext_occupancy_supplement, stay_ext_statutory_tax_charge, stay_ext_resort_credit_application and stay_ext_departure_balance_settlement, with post_occupancy_supplement_f6d09258, post_statutory_tax_charge_0b7e8f18, spend_resort_credit_ff384f87 (owner=user) and settle_departure_balance_f8243430, on the subjects stay_room_charge, stay_tax_and_fee_charge, stay_resort_credit_use and stay_check_out — the in-house and departure side. The two scopes share no policy, no tool and no subject, and between them they cover every extended policy this difficulty declares, which closes the suite at M=2.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD.
  Write subject stay_room_charge (step 7). Governing base policies: stay_agg_portfolio_occupancy, stay_room_and_occupancy and stay_club_and_corporate_interaction, none of which carries an eligibility gate, so each governs this write as scope. Inherited and not overridden: that occupancy limits and extra-occupant charges are counted per room and never across the portfolio; that a rate once sold is never re-priced; that a rollaway bed is charged per night at the plan's amount and a plan whose amount is zero provides it free; that a club discount and a corporate programme rate are mutually exclusive. Overridden once, and declared: base charges the plan's extra-adult amount for every night the occupant stays, whereas the extended rule charges the per-night supplement rate for the nights the folio has actually posted room lines for.
  Write subject stay_tax_and_fee_charge (step 9). Governing base policy: stay_taxes_and_fees, which carries no eligibility gate and so governs as scope. Inherited and not overridden: that taxes are calculated after any club or corporate discount has been applied to the room rate, so the discount reduces the tax as well; that the rate in force on the night stayed applies. Overridden once, and declared: base applies occupancy tax and city tax to the room total night by night, whereas the extended rule levies the two statutory rates together, once, on the whole taxable room money.
  Write subject stay_resort_credit_use (step 11). Governing base policy: stay_resort_credit. Gate guest_in_house (state; stay_reservations.status must read checked_in; authority system_record; correlated by stay_reservations.stay_reservation_id, bound to the tool's stay_reservation_id): true at the opening and still true at the moment of the write, because the departure write comes after it. Were the order reversed the reservation would already stand at checked_out and the gate would fail — which is the business reason the drawdown has to precede the settlement as well as the arithmetic one. Inherited and not overridden: that the credit is spent against charges taken at the property and never on the room rate, taxes or the agency service fee; that whatever is unspent at departure is forfeited without payment; that the credit lapses at the end of the plan's validity term counted from the arrival date. Overridden once, and declared: base places the credit for the plan's amount per stay, whereas the extended rule lets the grants posted for each room held stand together where the plan allows a companion to spend the credit.
  Write subject stay_check_out (step 13). Governing base policy: stay_incidentals, whose one gate stay_in_progress is scoped applies_to [stay_incidental_charge] and therefore does not apply to the departure write; it governs as scope. Inherited and not overridden: that a line disputed at departure is left on the folio and referred to the property desk. Overridden once, and declared: base settles every posted line against the deposit held, whereas the extended rule states the exact composition of the balance and adds the conversion markup at the end.
  Time anchors: this task exercises no time eligibility gate, so temporal_feasibility is empty. The one clock the calculations read is the credit validity term, and it is not a gate but an input: the plan's term is 5 calendar days from the arrival date of 2026-09-12, so the credit is available up to and including 2026-09-17; at 2026-09-16 the term has 1 day to run, at 2026-09-17 it would still be available and at 2026-09-18 the availability ladder would drop to its second tier and nothing could be drawn.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. The object is the Seattle reservation, correlated by stay_reservation_id. Rows entering the aggregates, on that reservation only: two deposit lines of 305.00 at room sequences 1 and 2, four room-night lines of 305.00 at night sequences 2 and 3 for both rooms, two property credit grants of 50.00 at room sequences 1 and 2 sharing the reference RC-AZUSEA-5581, and two minibar lines of 46.00 and 32.50 at occupant sequences 1 and 2. Rows excluded: every line of the Portland reservation — two room nights of 245.00, two occupancy taxes of 30.63, two city taxes of 9.80, two facility fees of 35.00 and one agency service fee of 12.95 — which share the customer but not the reservation. That exclusion is the sharpest trap in the task: a folio lookup by customer returns Portland's occupancy-tax lines alongside Seattle's untaxed folio, and an agent who reads "tax has been posted" from the customer's folio rather than this reservation's concludes the tax is already done and never discovers the second prerequisite at all. No derived row on the Seattle folio settles any other: there is no payout, no reversal and no drawdown standing against any grant.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root: stay_ext_departure_balance_settlement, the problem the caller's request points at ("the stay closed off properly and the balance taken off the card on file"). Three prerequisite problems, in a chain and a fan-in: the settlement waits on the statutory tax and on the credit drawdown, and the statutory tax waits on the occupant supplement.
  Edge stay_ext_statutory_tax_charge <- stay_ext_occupancy_supplement. kind value_input; gate is the tax rule's own compute binding supplement_total; form state. Sentence, verbatim from the tax rule: "The statutory tax due is settled only once the folio's room lines carry every occupant beyond the rate plan's standard occupancy for the nights of the stay already posted." Four-point test: the connective is "only once"; the side waited on is a record-visible state, namely room lines on the folio carrying the occupants beyond standard occupancy, in the words the folio lookup uses; no tool, policy id or code token appears; and its strength matches the edge exactly — a hard "only once", scoped to the nights already posted and no wider. State form was available and exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about: only stay_ext_occupancy_supplement books a line with charge_category extra_occupant, through post_occupancy_supplement_f6d09258. Derivation: the sentence says the tax waits on supplement lines; the folio shows room lines but none carrying a supplement; the only other rule in the corpus whose result is "the supplement charged for occupants beyond the standard occupancy of the rooms a guest holds" is the occupancy-supplement rule, so that is the write.
  Edge stay_ext_departure_balance_settlement <- stay_ext_statutory_tax_charge. kind value_input; gate is the settlement's binding tax_posted; form state. Sentence, verbatim from the settlement rule: "The balance settled at departure is struck only once the folio carries the statutory tax due on the room money for the stay." Four-point test: connective "only once"; a record-visible state (a statutory tax line on the folio); no code names; exactly the strength of the edge. Exactly one write books a line with charge_category occupancy_tax in this difficulty, namely the statutory tax rule's, through post_statutory_tax_charge_0b7e8f18.
  Edge stay_ext_departure_balance_settlement <- stay_ext_resort_credit_application. kind value_input; gate is the settlement's binding credit_drawn; form state. Sentence, verbatim from the settlement rule: "The balance settled at departure is struck only after the property credit standing on the reservation has been drawn down against the charges it may be spent against." Four-point test: connective "only after"; a record-visible state (credit drawn down on the reservation, which the folio shows as a drawdown line and the reservation as a smaller unspent balance); no code names; exactly the strength of the edge. Exactly one write books a line with charge_category resort_credit_use, namely the credit-application rule's, through spend_resort_credit_ff384f87, which is owner=user because base stay_resort_credit reserves the spending of property credit to the guest and the plan's transferability decides only who in the room may spend it. Neither of the two settlement sentences contains the other, and neither repeats the tax rule's sentence.
  Seed evidence that each is false at the opening is recorded per edge in prerequisite_closure. Topological order: occupancy supplement, statutory tax, credit drawdown, departure settlement. Parallel edges: the statutory tax and the credit drawdown hang side by side under the root and were replayed in both orders with identical terminal state and identical scored values, because neither rule reads a line the other writes and every row id is a content hash of its own arguments. Deletion sensitivity, from the Step 5 run: skipping the supplement moves the tax from 307.10 to 283.83; skipping the tax moves the balance from 2344.28 to 2029.50; skipping the drawdown moves it to 2424.74.

WORLD, ROW BY ROW, AND WHAT EACH ROW CARRIES.
  customers: one traveller. His mobile number and passport last four are the two details the identity check needs; he explicitly cannot produce a third, so a real agent pressing for one gets a definite answer rather than improvisation.
  stay_reservations: two. The Seattle reservation is the object of the call and stands at checked in with four nights, two rooms, five adults and 100.00 of property credit unspent; the property facility fee the plan does not waive stands on it per room per night for the nights already covered. The Portland reservation is closed and carries nine folio lines including its own occupancy and city taxes; remove it and no scored value changes, which is exactly its job.
  stay_folio_entries, Seattle: two deposit lines covering the first night of each room — remove them and the room money, the booked nightly rate and the deposit offset all move. Four room-night lines for nights two and three — with night one's room money standing on the deposit lines, the nights of the stay already covered on the folio are three, which is the highest night sequence the room lines carry, against the four the stay covers; that gap is what three separate ladders read. Two property credit grants, one per room, sharing one credit reference — remove one and the credit standing falls to 50.00 and the drawdown with it. Two minibar lines at different occupant sequences — remove the second and the eligible-spend ladder drops to its lead-guest tier. Every one of these lines is in Canadian dollars on the room money side and US dollars on the property side, which is what puts the settlement on its markup tier.
  stay_folio_entries, Portland: two room nights, two occupancy taxes, two city taxes, two facility fees and one agency service fee — the excludable trap described above.
  club_memberships: one active Wanderlane Platinum card, which puts the tax computation on a 6 percent room-money discount; remove it and the tax rises to 326.70.
  Automatic-clause check: the stay charter's automatic consequences are the triggers on stay_confirm, stay_cancel, stay_no_show, stay_check_in and stay_check_out. The Seattle reservation is confirmed and checked in, so its deposit charge and its credit grants are already posted and nothing further is lit; it is not cancelled and not a no-show. The Portland reservation is closed with its lines settled. No stale statistic cache is designed here: stay_reservations.folio_balance_usd agrees with the sum of the money lines on each reservation (1908.50 and 653.81) and resort_credit_balance_usd agrees with the two grants (100.00). The history difficulty comes from separating two reservations, four charge categories and two occupant sequences, not from a cache trap.
  No field anywhere names a factor's outcome: there is no "supplement due" flag, no "tax posted" marker and no cached tier. The club tier is read from the membership's variant_name and its hotel rate discount from the club charter's own tier parameters; the standard occupancy, the nights charged, the rollaway component, the taxability of the supplement, the statutory rate, the credit standing, its availability, the countability of the minibar, the eligible spend, the room money measure, the inclusion of the tax and of the on-property charges, the two offsets and the markup are all derived from rows.

PERSONA. Ntando is easy-going, standing in a lobby with his bags down, and wants the thing finished before he drives off; the voice is unhurried and faintly amused at his own ignorance of rate plans. He volunteers only three things: the goal (he is leaving today, close the stay off, take the balance, tell him the figure first), that this is for now rather than later, and his authorisation boundary (the desk may do whatever it needs to, and anything it cannot do he will do himself on the spot). Everything else comes only on being asked: the mobile number, the passport last four, which stay he means and its confirmation number, five adults across two rooms with no children, that there was a minibar bill he cannot put a number to, and — for the question a real agent always asks and gold never records — that the balance goes on the same card as the deposit and is not to be split. His one refusal is prepared: he cannot remember which email he booked with and will not guess. His passive reactions fire on utterance events, never on the records: he agrees when told something has to go onto the bill first, he laughs and runs the drawdown only after the agent explains it has to come from him, and he closes by repeating the balance back once when told it. He never names an amount, never mentions tax or a supplement before the agent does, never asks whether something must be sorted out first, and never corrects a wrong step.

REACHABILITY IN ONE CONVERSATION. Turn by turn: he states the goal and his mobile number; the desk locates and verifies him on the mobile number and the passport last four; the desk reads both reservations and fixes on Seattle from the city, the room count, the night count and the confirmation number; the desk reads the whole folio and sees the deposits, the four room nights, the two credit grants and the two minibar lines, and sees that no supplement, no tax and no drawdown stand; the desk reads the club membership; the desk prices and posts the supplement, then the tax; the desk explains the credit has to be spent by him, hands it over, and his receipt enters the conversation; the desk then strikes the balance and closes the stay off; he repeats the figure and rings off. Every fact used is on the records at the opening, stated by him when asked, or produced by a preceding call in this same conversation. Nothing waits on anything outside the lobby: no property has to confirm anything, no card has to clear, no review has to be approved and no date has to arrive. All four writes execute at the one frozen_time 2026-09-16 11:05:00 UTC, and the order among them expresses causation only.

WHAT A CARELESS AGENT GETS WRONG, AND HOW THE POLICY EXCLUDES IT. Reading the folio by customer and seeing Portland's occupancy-tax lines, then concluding the tax is done. Taking the standard occupancy as 3 adults a room and finding no supplement at all. Counting only the two occupants the folio's charges stand against rather than the five adults declared, and again finding no supplement. Charging the supplement for all four nights instead of the three posted. Forgetting that the plan charges for a rollaway bed, which halves the per-night rate. Counting none of the supplement as room money for tax. Grossing the room money up to four nights while the guest is still in house. Forgetting the club discount before tax, or applying it after. Treating the credit as one grant of 50.00 rather than one per room. Drawing the credit against the room money rather than the charges taken at the property. Charging only the room lines posted at departure and omitting the night that has not posted. Forgetting to set the deposit or the drawn credit against the balance. Leaving the property facility fee off the balance although it stands on the folio and the plan does not waive it. Forgetting the conversion markup on money taken in Canadian dollars. Each of these is excluded by a sentence of the published terms read against a row of the folio, not by judgement.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate and verify. Read the reservations; pick Seattle. Read the folio; separate the Seattle lines. Read the club card. Price the supplement: standard occupancy 2 a room, all five adults counted because the folio's charges stand against two occupants, one occupant beyond the four covered, three nights posted, 50.00 a night, 150.00. Price the tax: room money posted 1830.00 plus the whole 150.00 supplement, no gross-up while in house, less 6 percent, at 16.5 percent, 307.10. Hand the credit drawdown to the guest: credit standing 100.00, wholly available, minibar 78.50 wholly countable and wholly eligible, so 78.50. Strike the balance: room money 2590.00 including the night not yet covered, plus 307.10 of tax, plus 174.00 of property facility fee, plus 78.50 of on-property charges, less 78.50 of credit, less 610.00 of deposit, plus 2.5 percent markup, 2522.63. Close the stay off.

VERIFICATION ACTUALLY RUN. The handling-time recomputations, the per-factor baseline substitutions and the three prerequisite-skip replays were executed against this exact initial_state with the gate's own evaluator (build_env / eval_compute / substitute from skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/check_compute.py), replaying each write with the real tool between computations. Output: supplement result=150.00 (bindings 14, branches 10, history rows 8) with deposit_rooms 2, standard_adults_per_room 2, folio_occupants 2, counted_adults 5, extra_adults 1, folio_nights 3, nights_charged 3, rollaway_posted 0, per_night_rate 50.00; per-factor baselines 0.00 (standard_occupancy), 0.00 (party_spread), 200.00 (nights_convention), 75.00 (rollaway_component) and all four together 0.00. Statutory tax result=307.10 (bindings 16, branches 12, history rows 7) with room_lines_total 1830.00, supplement_total 150.00, supplement_taxable_pct 100, room_money 1980.00, club_status active, room_discount_pct 6, taxable_room_money 1861.20, stay_elapsed_days 4, statutory_rate_pct 16.5; per-factor baselines 283.83, 326.70, 409.46, 232.65 and all four together 305.00. Credit drawdown result=78.50 (bindings 16, branches 10, history rows 4) with grant_posted 100.00, grant_rooms 2, lead_grant 50.00, credit_standing 100.00, credit_valid_days 4, availability_pct 100, minibar_posted 78.50, minibar_occupants 2, lead_guest_minibar 46.00, eligible_spend 78.50; per-factor baselines 50.00 (credit_grant_measure), 0.00, 0.00, 0.00 and all four together 0.00. Departure balance result=2522.63 (bindings 25, branches 14, history rows 17) with booked_nightly_rate 305.00, room_money_charged 2590.00, tax_charged 307.10, facility_posted 174.00, onproperty_charged 78.50, credit_offset 78.50, deposit_offset 610.00, presented_currency CAD, markup_pct 2.5, gross_balance 2461.10; per-factor baselines 1897.38, 2207.85, 2442.16, 2603.09, 3147.88, 2461.10 and all six together 2154.00. Prerequisite skips: 283.83, 2207.85 and 2603.09. Every one of these figures differs from the scored value, so no factor and no edge is decoration. The per-task gates check_extended, check_task_tools, replay_tasks, check_solvability, check_compute, check_grounding and check_cross_fire were then run on --task 1 and are green.

RULE AND COMPUTE, BOTH WAYS. Forward: every binding of all four policies that reads the world, aggregates, chooses, crosses a category, caps or rounds carries a verbatim quotation of the rule sentence it implements in compute_basis, and each of the eighteen ladder bindings quotes its ladder sentence in full. Backward: sweeping each rule, the supplement rule's sentences about the standard occupancy, the occupants the supplement is counted for, the occupants beyond standard occupancy, the nights charged, the per-night rate, the product and the floor are implemented by standard_adults_per_room, counted_adults, extra_adults, nights_charged, per_night_rate and result; the tax rule's sentences about the room money posted, the share of the supplement counted, the gross-up, the discount, the statutory rate and the rounding are implemented by room_lines_total, supplement_taxable_pct, room_money, room_discount_pct, statutory_rate_pct and result; the credit rule's sentences about the credit standing, its availability, the countability of the minibar, the eligible spend and the smaller of the two are implemented by credit_standing, availability_pct, minibar_counted_pct, eligible_spend and result; the settlement rule's sentences about the nights already covered, the booked nightly rate, the room money charged, the property facility fee charged in full, the four shares, the composition and the markup are implemented by folio_nights, booked_nightly_rate, room_money_charged, facility_posted, tax_included_pct, onproperty_pct, credit_offset_pct, deposit_offset_pct, gross_balance and result. The sensitive words check out: "the nights of the stay already covered on the folio", which each rule defines outright as the highest night sequence the folio's room lines carry, carries exactly that MAX over night_sequence with a charge_category filter; "counted charges standing against the lead guest's own occupant sequence" carries a guest_sequence filter; "the largest single grant posted" carries MAX; "the smaller of" carries MN; "never less than nothing" carries MX against zero; "rounded to two decimal places" carries RND. No filter appears in an expression that the quoted sentence does not state.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT. Masking the extended yaml, compute, expected, gold and this dossier, and working only from the prose that will be published, the tool schemas, what the share tools return and what the caller actually says: the guest is departing a stay that still stands at checked in; the published terms say the balance settled at departure is struck only once the folio carries the statutory tax due on the room money, and only after the property credit standing has been drawn down; this folio carries neither, so both have to be settled first. The tax terms in turn say the tax is settled only once the room lines carry every occupant beyond standard occupancy, and the folio carries no supplement line while five adults are declared against two rooms — so the supplement comes first of all. Working the three sets of terms on the visible folio gives 150.00, then 307.10, then 78.50, and the settlement terms then give 2590.00 + 307.10 + 174.00 + 78.50 - 78.50 - 610.00 = 2461.10 at 102.5 percent, that is 2522.63. That is gold. The only places a second reading could arise — which reservation, which credit reference, whether the unposted night is charged and whether the supplement is taxable — are each pinned by an explicit sentence or by the caller's own answer.

REVISIONS. (0) Symptom: the supplement rule's second factor originally decided the occupants beyond standard occupancy by choosing between the rooms the folio carries room lines for and the rooms held, and in this world those are both 2, so an honest baseline (the formula the computation document states) left the number unchanged and the factor was decoration. Root cause: the two tiers were distinguished by a quantity the seed makes equal. Change: the factor now decides the occupants the supplement is counted for — every adult declared where the folio's charges stand against more than one occupant, the occupants the folio shows otherwise — and the computation document states the latter as its standard method. Re-run: the tier taken gives 5 counted adults and 1 beyond standard occupancy, the baseline gives 2 counted adults and none beyond, so the supplement moves from 150.00 to 0.00; the scored value is unchanged. Propagated to the rule prose, the ladder, compute, compute_basis, the factor card, the factor trace and the argument tracing at step 6. (0b) Symptom: the credit rule's first factor declared a baseline of the largest single grant while its computation document said the credit standing was the grant posted together with whatever had been drawn — a baseline that was not what the document states. Change: the document sentence now reads "the largest single grant posted on the reservation together with whatever has already been drawn against it", and the factor's baseline is that same expression. Re-run: baseline 50.00 against a scored 78.50, so the factor still bears weight. (1) Symptom: the credit rule first multiplied a single 50.00 grant by the rooms held, which left the reservation's unspent-credit field at -28.50 after the drawdown — a terminal state no folio could show. Root cause: the grant was seeded once per stay while the rule reasoned per room. Change: the seed now carries one grant of 50.00 per room held, both under the single reference RC-AZUSEA-5581, and the reservation's unspent credit opens at 100.00; the credit-standing ladder now chooses between the grants taken together and the largest single grant, according to whether the plan lets a companion spend the credit. Re-run: credit standing 100.00, drawdown 78.50, unspent credit 21.50 afterwards, and the factor still moves the number (baseline 50.00). Propagated to the overwrite declaration, the rule prose, the ladder, the factor card, the argument tracing and the seed-consistency entry for the grant lines. (2) Symptom: the eligible-spend ladder originally tiered on the same transferability flag as the credit-standing ladder, repeating one condition across two factors. Change: it now tiers on the occupant sequences the minibar charges stand against and on the adults declared against the rooms held, which is fresh evidence. Re-run: the tier taken and the scored value are unchanged at 78.50, and the factor's baseline is still 0.00. (3) ROUND 2, against env/online_travel_agency/audits/policy_task/hotel_reservations_desk/1.md and _difficulty.md. F-4/T1 (red): three rules said "the nights the folio carries room lines for" while compute returned MAX(night_sequence) over the room lines — a count against a high-water ordinal. On this folio night one's room money stands on the deposit lines, so the count is two and the ordinal is three, and the two readings gave 150.00 / 307.10 / 2344.28 against 100.00 / 299.34 / 3535.57. Root cause: the prose named a count and the expression returned an ordinal, in a charter that elsewhere names ordinals explicitly ("the highest room sequence the prepayment lines were posted for"). Change: all three rules now name the quantity "the nights of the stay already covered on the folio" and each defines it outright — "The nights of the stay already covered on the folio are taken as the highest night sequence the folio's room lines carry." — so prose and expression denote the same thing by definition; the ladder tiers, the compute_basis quotations, the gross-up sentence and the booked-nightly-rate sentence were reworded in the same pass, and the definition sits in each baseline.rule so the computation document carries it too. Re-run: D 150.00 and C 307.10 are unchanged, every factor baseline is unchanged, and the division in booked_nightly_rate is now stated over the same three nights its numerator covers. F-11 (observation): the Member Flex Rate does not waive the property facility fee, yet no resort_fee line stood on the Seattle folio while the guest's own Portland folio carried one per night. Change: the facility fee is now seeded per room per night for the three nights already covered (six lines of 29.00, 174.00 in all, folio balance 2082.50), and the settlement charges it through a plumbing binding facility_posted with one sentence in the rule and in the baseline. Re-run: the scored balance moves from 2344.28 to 2522.63 and all six of its factors still move it; D, C and B are untouched because none of their bindings reads resort_fee. F-8 (observation): the credit edge's sentence was a perfect passive of the depended-on action; it now reads "The balance settled at departure is struck only once the folio carries the property credit drawn down against the charges it may be spent against.", the state construction its three sibling edges use, and prerequisite_closure's policy_source carries the new wording. F-5 (observation): the rule promised "the largest single grant posted together with whatever has already been drawn against it" on the credit-standing ladder's second and third tiers while compute implemented bare lead_grant; both branches now read RND(lead_grant + credit_drawn_already, 2), which is also the factor's declared baseline. No number moves (nothing had been drawn), and the declared baseline is now literally the compute's fall-through. F-9 (observation): party_spread and credit_grant_measure swap an aggregate rather than a number and are relabelled method, their ladder tiers rewritten as methods; stay_ext_occupancy_supplement and stay_ext_resort_credit_application each now stand at 2 parameter and 2 method, inside the bounds.
user_scenario:
Ntando Mkhwebane is a Cape Town structural engineer, forty and unhurried, who has spent four nights in Seattle with two colleagues and their partners across two rooms and is due to leave this morning. He rings the Wanderlane desk from the lobby with his bags already down, cheerful and a little apologetic about the noise around him, because the property's front desk has told him his bill is not closed off and that the agency holds the booking. What he asks for is plain: he is leaving today, he would like the stay closed off properly and the balance taken off the card on file, and he would like to be told what that figure is before he gets in the car. He is happy for the desk to sort out whatever it needs to sort out on his behalf and says so without being asked twice; anything the desk cannot do for him he will do himself, there and then, while he is still standing in the lobby. This is not a query for later — he wants it done now.

When the desk asks how to find him he gives his mobile number, 7020863419, and when a second thing on file is wanted he reads out the last four of his passport, 2907. He cannot remember which email he used to book and says so rather than guessing, and he would rather not be kept hunting for it; those two will have to do. Asked which stay he means, he says the Seattle one, two rooms, four nights, checking out today, and the confirmation is PH36DTL9. Asked about the party he says there are five adults across the two rooms — one of his colleagues brought his brother at the last minute — and no children. Asked whether anyone charged anything to the rooms he says yes, there was a minibar bill, he thinks from both rooms, and he has no idea what it comes to. If he is asked how he wants the balance taken he says on the same card as the deposit, which was in Canadian dollars because his firm's card is issued in Toronto, and no, he does not want it split.

He has never read a rate plan in his life and says as much with some amusement.
